idiom_name: class holding the invariant + namespace-scoped helpers found by ADL (C++ Core Guidelines C.2/C.4/C.5)
implementation_notes: The class is the language's native contour: declare the state together with the operations that maintain it (use class when there is an invariant, struct when the members vary independently - C.2) and let access control hide the representation. C++ refines where each operation goes: make a function a member only when it needs the representation (C.4), and place the remaining helpers and operators in the class's namespace so argument-dependent lookup finds them (C.5); the full-member classic form is still right when the operation enforces an invariant or touches private state.
pitfalls: Public getters and setters for every field reproduce the anemic model inside a class: they publish the representation and let clients bypass the operations that guard the invariants.
Non-member helpers must live in the class's namespace; in the global namespace they lose ADL and the concept stops being discoverable.
Free functions that need private state force friend declarations or pimpl plumbing, which widens the boundary; redesign them against the public API instead.
